items.title: November 24, 2026
items.summary: BigQueryFeatureThe following table-valued functions are nowgenerally available(GA) in the query editor and as part ofconversational analyticsto help you analyze your data:ML.TREND:identify the directional trajectory of your data.ML.SEASONALITY:identify repeating patterns in your data.ML.DETECT_CHANGE_POINTS:identify intervals where structural shifts occur in your data.ML.CORRELATION:identify the statistical correlation between a target column and one or moremetric columns.FeatureThe built-in text embedding model embeddinggemma-300m in theAI.EMBEDandAI.SIMILARITYfunctions isgenerally available(GA).FeatureBigQuery Migration Service supports translating Databricks SQL and ApacheSpark SQL 3.x and 4.x into GoogleSQL and extracting schema metadata fromDatabricks inPreview.For more information, seeDatabricks and Apache Spark SQL translation referenceandSupported SQL dialects.Google SecOps SIEMDeprecatedThese SIEM Release Notes are now deprecated. For future updates on new features, changes, and announcements, see Google SecOps Release Notes.Google SecOps SOARDeprecatedThese SOAR Release Notes are now deprecated. For future updates on new features, changes, and announcements, see Google SecOps Release Notes.Managed Service for Apache AirflowAnnouncementIn December 2026, new Managed Airflow images and builds will no longerpre-install site-packages/ray/jars/ray_dist.jar, the Java runtime that Rayuses for Java and cross-language (Python-Java) workloads:Python-only Ray workloads are unaffected by this change.Remote Java or cross-language Ray jobs submitted to an external cluster (suchas Ray on Vertex AI or KubeRay on GKE) are unaffected because they use theray_dist.jar inside the remote cluster image, not the environment's localcopy.Only workloads that start a local Java or cross-language Ray runtime directlyinside the Airflow worker, or custom code directly readingsite-packages/ray/jars/ray_dist.jar, might require action.Existing environments will be affected by this change when you upgrade themto a version or build that doesn't have ray/jars/ray_dist.jarpre-installed.If you start a local Java or cross-language Ray runtime directly inside anAirflow worker, you will need to manually supply the missing runtime library.Follow these steps:Extract ray_dist.jar from the exact version of the ray package installedin your environment. For the list of packages in your environment, seePreinstalled packages changelog.Upload the extracted ray_dist.jar to the data/ folder of yourManaged Airflow environment's bucket.Add the JAR file path to your Ray jobs using Ray's native java_jarsruntime environment configuration option.AnnouncementIn December 2026, Managed Airflow (Gen 3) and Managed Airflow (Gen 2)environments will start using Python 3.12:New Airflow builds of Managed Airflow (Gen 3) and versions ofManaged Airflow (Gen 2) will switch to Python 3.12.Python 3.11.8 will no longer be available in new versions and Airflow buildsof Managed Airflow.Existing Managed Airflow (Gen 3) environments will keep using Python 3.11.8until you manually upgrade the Airflow build of your environment to a buildthat uses Python 3.12.Existing Managed Airflow (Gen 2) environments will keep using Python 3.11.8until you manually upgrade your environment to a version that usesPython 3.12.Managed Airflow (Gen 3) builds and Managed Airflow (Gen 2) versions releasedbefore this change will keep using Python 3.11.8.NetApp VolumesAnnouncementThe Flex File service level for Google Cloud NetApp Volumes is no longeravailable in the following regions:asia-east2 (Hong Kong)europe-central2 (Warsaw)europe-west6 (Zurich)europe-west10 (Berlin)northamerica-south1 (Querétaro)us-south1 (Dallas)Other service levels remain available in europe-west6 (Standard, Premium, andExtreme) and us-south1 (Flex Unified). For more information about availableregions, seeSupported regions.
